chapter: Chapter 3. The kinetic theory of an ideal gas
title: Boltzmann's constant

prose.text:
In equation $(3-14)$, the ratio of the universal gas constant $R$ to Avogadro's constant $N_A$ does not depend on the substance.
This ratio is called **Boltzmann's constant**, named after the Austrian physicist Boltzmann, one of the founders of kinetic theory.
The constant is universal, but the earlier classical formula for average kinetic energy still has conditions: it cannot be applied without limits to every state of matter.
prose.source_text: 在方程 $(3-14)$ 中含有一个气体普适恒量 $R$ 和阿伏伽德罗常数 $N_A$ 的比值。对于所有物质来说，这个比值都是相同的。为了对奥地利学者、分子运动论奠基者之一的玻尔兹曼表示尊敬，把这个比值叫做玻尔兹曼恒量。

historical_entities.reason: p0085#3 原文的阿伏伽德罗常数命名，保留实际源译名及真实人物身份。
p0085#3 原文说明恒量以玻尔兹曼命名，保留该真实物理学家的身份。

prose.text: Using the rounded values given in the textbook, Boltzmann's constant is:

historical_entities.reason: p0085#4 原文以真实物理学家命名的恒量，保持原有科学名称。

prose.text: $k=\frac{R}{N_A}=\frac{8.31\frac{\text{J}}{\text{K}\cdot\text{mol}}}{6.02\times10^{23}\frac{1}{\text{mol}}}$ $=1.38\times10^{-23}$ J/K.
prose.source_text: $k=\frac{R}{N_A}=\frac{8.31\frac{\text{焦耳}}{\text{开}\cdot\text{摩尔}}}{6.02\times10^{23}\frac{1}{\text{摩尔}}}$ $=1.38\times10^{-23}$ 焦耳/开。

prose.text:
Using Boltzmann's constant, equation $(3-14)$ takes the following form.
We are considering a classical ideal gas in thermal equilibrium, with absolute temperature measured in kelvins.

Here, average kinetic energy means the energy of the molecules' irregular motion through space.
It does not include the energy of the gas flowing as a whole, or energy from molecular rotation or internal vibration.

Boltzmann ($1844\sim1906$) was an Austrian physicist and one of the founders of kinetic theory.
The textbook emphasizes his papers' contribution to developing kinetic theory into a systematic account.
prose.source_text: $L.$ 玻尔兹曼（$1844\sim1906$）——伟大的奥地利物理学家，分子运动论奠基者之一。在玻尔兹曼的论文中，首先提出了分子运动论作为合理的、严整的、连续的物理理论。

prose.text:
According to the textbook, he argued that molecular motion and collisions explain thermal phenomena.
He took part in the scientific debate about whether molecules exist.
prose.source_text: 自然科学的战士，他热情地提出热现象分子碰撞的必要性，并与反对存在有分子的学者进行了斗争。

prose.text:
Substituting equation $(3.15)$ into formula $(3.11)$ gives a relation between gas pressure, molecular number density, and absolute temperature.
Molecular number density means the number of molecules in each unit of volume, not the total number in the whole sample.
This relation still uses the classical ideal-gas model in thermal equilibrium:
prose.source_text: 把 $(3.15)$ 式代到公式 $(3.11)$ 中，得到气体压强与分子密度和温度关系的表示式：

prose.text:
This gives Avogadro's law for ideal gases: at the same pressure and absolute temperature, different gases have the same molecular number density.
Equal volumes therefore contain equal numbers of molecules (see section $16$).
Real gases obey this conclusion approximately only where the ideal-gas approximation applies.
prose.source_text: 特别是，由此可以得出阿伏加德罗定律：在同压同温下，所有气体的分子密度都相同，因此，在相同的体积中包含有相同的分子数（参阅 § $16$）。

historical_entities.reason: p0086#3 原文的阿伏加德罗定律命名；保留此处实际源译名及真实人物身份。

prose.text:
At the textbook's standard state ($p=101325$ N/m$^2$ and $T=273K$), the ideal-gas model gives the number of molecules in $1$ cubic centimeter of gas from the number density below.
The temperature and constants use the textbook's stated precision:
prose.source_text: 在标准状态下（$p=101325$ 牛顿/米$^2$ 和 $T=273K$），$1$ 立方厘米任意气体的分子数等于

prose.text: $n=\frac{p}{kT}=\frac{101325\frac{\text{N}}{\text{m}^2}}{1.38\times10^{-23}\frac{\text{J}}{\text{K}}}\cdot\frac{1}{273\ \text{K}}$ $=2.69\times10^{19}$ cm$^{-3}$.

The calculation uses meters, so its result is first a number of molecules per cubic meter.
One cubic meter contains a million cubic centimeters.
Divide the per-cubic-meter density by a million to express it per cubic centimeter.

The textbook calls this number density at its standard state the **Loschmidt number**.
It is a number per unit volume, not the total number of molecules in any chosen sample.
To obtain the total number, multiply the number density by the sample's volume, using matching volume units.
prose.source_text: 这个数叫做洛喜密脱数。

historical_entities.reason: p0086#6 原文的洛喜密脱数命名，保留真实历史人物的实际源译名。

prose.text:
The textbook traces the historical sequence: scientists first established a temperature scale, then explained temperature's microscopic meaning (see section $11$).
In the classical model of thermal equilibrium used here, average kinetic energy from motion through space can be measured in joules or ergs.
The quantity $T^*$ uses that energy to describe the same thermal state as the absolute temperature $T$ measured in kelvins.

This expresses temperature on an energy scale;
it does not make the kelvin an energy unit.
In the next formula, the mass is the mass of one molecule, and speeds are measured in a reference frame where the gas as a whole is at rest:
prose.source_text: 在历史上，温度是第一个作为热力学量引入的，并建立了测量温度的单位——度（参阅 § $11$）。在说明了温度与分子平均动能的关系之后，很显然，可以用温度来量度分子的平均动能，用焦耳或尔格来量度温度，即用量值 $T^*$ 代替量值 $T$，则

prose.text: $T^*=\frac{m\overline{v^2}}{2}.$
This energy quantity, defined as the average kinetic energy from molecular motion through space, is related to the absolute temperature measured in kelvins by:
prose.source_text: 这样定义的温度是与用度来量度的温度有联系的：

prose.text:
Boltzmann's constant connects absolute temperature with a microscopic energy scale.
For this average kinetic energy, multiply Boltzmann's constant by the absolute temperature and then by three halves.

Temperature is usually expressed in temperature units;
this lesson's formulas use kelvins.
An energy-scale variable depends on the specified model and scaling, so its definition and conditions must be stated.
prose.source_text: 因此，可以把玻尔兹曼恒量看作是联系用能量单位表示的温度与用度测量的温度的量。不过，习惯上广泛采用以度来测量温度。

data.title: 玻尔兹曼恒量

prose.text: 在方程 $(3-14)$ 中含有一个气体普适恒量 $R$ 和阿伏伽德罗常数 $N_A$ 的比值。对于所有物质来说，这个比值都是相同的。为了对奥地利学者、分子运动论奠基者之一的玻尔兹曼表示尊敬，把这个比值叫做玻尔兹曼恒量。
玻尔兹曼恒量等于
$k=\frac{R}{N_A}=\frac{8.31\frac{\text{焦耳}}{\text{开}\cdot\text{摩尔}}}{6.02\times10^{23}\frac{1}{\text{摩尔}}}$ $=1.38\times10^{-23}$ 焦耳/开。
考虑到玻尔兹曼恒量，方程 $(3-14)$ 可写成
$\overline E=\frac{3}{2}kT.$　$(3-15)$
$L.$ 玻尔兹曼（$1844\sim1906$）——伟大的奥地利物理学家，分子运动论奠基者之一。在玻尔兹曼的论文中，首先提出了分子运动论作为合理的、严整的、连续的物理理论。
玻尔兹曼在发展和普及麦克斯韦电磁场理论方面做了很多工作。
自然科学的战士，他热情地提出热现象分子碰撞的必要性，并与反对存在有分子的学者进行了斗争。
把 $(3.15)$ 式代到公式 $(3.11)$ 中，得到气体压强与分子密度和温度关系的表示式：
特别是，由此可以得出阿伏加德罗定律：在同压同温下，所有气体的分子密度都相同，因此，在相同的体积中包含有相同的分子数（参阅 § $16$）。
在标准状态下（$p=101325$ 牛顿/米$^2$ 和 $T=273K$），$1$ 立方厘米任意气体的分子数等于
$n=\frac{p}{kT}=\frac{101325\frac{\text{牛顿}}{\text{米}^2}}{1.38\times10^{-23}\frac{\text{焦耳}}{\text{开}}}\cdot\frac{1}{273\ \text{开}}$ $=2.69\times10^{19}$ 厘米$^{-3}$。
这个数叫做洛喜密脱数。
在历史上，温度是第一个作为热力学量引入的，并建立了测量温度的单位——度（参阅 § $11$）。在说明了温度与分子平均动能的关系之后，很显然，可以用温度来量度分子的平均动能，用焦耳或尔格来量度温度，即用量值 $T^*$ 代替量值 $T$，则
$T^*=\frac{m\overline{v^2}}{2}.$
这样定义的温度是与用度来量度的温度有联系的：
因此，可以把玻尔兹曼恒量看作是联系用能量单位表示的温度与用度测量的温度的量。不过，习惯上广泛采用以度来测量温度。
